post.summary: Open the project's native Session, or name the live one
post.description: Only on a server its operator started with sessions (health capability `sessionHost`). The Session opens as bare `nika` opens it in the server's project: the server's kept intelligence choice and census, its HOME history (recovery notice and restored state in `notices`). One live Session per project: its history is one per (HOME, project). A second open answers 409 `session_live` with the live Session's identity to attach to. A history held elsewhere (a terminal Session on that project) answers 409 `session_unavailable` with the Session's own refusal. No field names a path, a model, a provider or a key.

intelligence.description: The intelligence this conversation selects, in the census's own first-screen words (`1 [acp:]<app>[/<model>]`, `2 [<provider>[/<model>]]`, `3 [<engine>[/<model>]]`, `4`), resolved against this server's census and configuration. It holds for this conversation only: the server's kept choice is neither read nor written. Words the census does not read answer 409 `session_unavailable` with its fix. Never an endpoint or a key.

get.description: Never waits on a turn: `snapshot.busy` names the command under way, its phase (`preparing`, `running`, `stopping`: the run took its first signal, `settling`) and whether a Stop was taken for it (`stop_requested`).

404.description: A `refused` frame: session_not_found (unknown, closed, or another incarnation)

delete.description: A preparation under way is stopped, nothing more is admitted, the turn under way settles, the runtime releases its history, and `closed` ends the log. A Run under way is not stopped by closing: the close waits for it (a `stop` command asks it to stop first).

get.summary: The details card of the current snapshot
get.description: The Session's own `/details` text, captured when that snapshot was published; it answers while a provider call runs and stops nothing.

post.summary: Submit a line against a snapshot, answer one question it asks, stop the turn under way, or queue a line for the conversation's run under way
post.description: A submit reaches the Session only when it names the CURRENT snapshot; the Session receives that snapshot's retained `Waiting`, never one rebuilt from the request. An `answer` (`question` and `line`) or a `delegate` (`question` alone) reaches the one question its identity names among those the CURRENT snapshot asks (`work.waiting.id`, each of `work.waiting.ids`, an open choice of `work.open_choices` while a proposal waits, or the optional offer about the last result, `work.feedback.offer.question.id`, while nothing else waits), through the Session's identity door, and the other questions keep waiting: nothing reads which question a line answers. A `delegate` leaves the choice to Nika, never as words: the question's recommended offer is bound as delegated, or, with none, the author chooses; a question the compiler asks takes no delegation (its result is a `wrong_state` refusal). An identity that snapshot does not ask answers 409 unknown_question before anything reaches the Session: one an earlier snapshot asked (answered, dropped or replaced since), or one this Session never asked. A command identity already known answers first: the same bytes (op, snapshot, question, line) return the recorded result with `replayed: true` (an original still running is awaited, never run twice); other bytes answer 409 command_conflict. One turn at a time: a submit during a turn answers 409 busy with its line returned unconsumed. The answer to a submit comes once it settled; no request deadline applies, and a disconnected request never cancels the accepted turn. A stop answers at once with its receipt; the settlement is the target command's own result. `stop_requested`: the preparation under way stops, or the Run it executes had not started its work yet (it starts none, or takes the Stop as it starts). `run_stopping`: the Run took its first signal, as a first Ctrl-C sends it: in-flight work completes and is counted, except an MCP call under way, which is stopped (its server is told to cancel it) and named in the settlement's `stopped_calls`, an effect's outcome unknown when the call had been sent; no new wave starts, and its result carries `run_stopped` once its trace sealed as cancelled (`run_aborted` when it ended without sealing it). `nothing_to_stop`: no turn, the turn is settling, or its Run already ended. `run_underway`: this door cannot stop the Run. A replayed stop answers its recorded receipt, and a second stop while one is under way sends nothing more: a stop never escalates to an abort. A `steer` (the line enters after the calls under way) or a `follow_up` (it enters when the run would end) answers at once with its receipt: `queued` with the line's identity and state (`queued`), `not_reading` (a turn runs that no conversation's run reads: send the line once it settled), `nothing_to_steer` (no turn: submit the line), `blank`, `full` (the run took as many lines as it takes: send the line once it ended); what became of each queued line is in the snapshot's `busy.queued` while the run reads it, then in the work's `queued`.

409.description: A `refused` frame: stale_snapshot, unknown_snapshot, unknown_question, busy or command_conflict

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: `<session>:<event>` of this Session: the stream resumes after that event. Any other value (another Session or incarnation, beyond the log) gets one `resync` frame with the current snapshot, then the live events.

get.summary: The Session's log as server-sent events
get.description: Each event's `id` is `<session>:<event>` and its `data` one frame that carries `event`. The stream ends after `closed`. Aborting the stream stops nothing.

SessionCommand.description: One command of the contract: each op takes exactly its own fields, and a missing or any other field is refused malformed.

SessionCommandIdentity.description: the caller's identity for this command

SessionSnapshotHandle.description: the handle of the snapshot the line was typed against, or the question read in

SessionQuestionIdentity.description: the identity of one question that snapshot asks, as its work states it

seq.description: publish order, distinct from event numbers

queued.description: the lines queued for the conversation's run while it reads them

work.description: The Session's `nika/session-work@0` snapshot, verbatim: `root` names the server's project world, paths are relative to it. While a refused knowledge source holds a line, `waiting` is `{"kind": "knowledge_choice", "line": <the line, exactly as typed>}`: nothing was sent for it, and submitting `/knowledge embedded` resumes it once.

SessionKnowledge.description: The authoring knowledge the Session reads now, a configured fact and never a call receipt: `admitted` (a release the strict door admitted: `source` `embedded` or `disk`, its `version`, its `manifest_sha256`, and `by` `default`, `conversation`, `host` or `environment`), `refused` (a source the configuration names, refused: `source` `snapshot`, `pack` or `embedded`, `by`, the stable `code` and its `cause`, never a host path; a line that would reach a model waits as `knowledge_choice`), or `unread` (`why`: knowledge off, the strategy `off`, or a configuration refused before its knowledge resolved).

SessionQueued.description: One line the person sent while the conversation's run was under way: its identity (`l1`, `l2`, …), how it waits, the words, and what became of it — `waiting`, `entered` (it became the person's line `cite`), `returned` (unsent: the run stopped, waited for the person or ended before reading it).

SessionCall.description: One physical model call an activity frame reports: its rank, the compiler's or conversation's role, the REQUESTED model (never proof of the served one), `started`, `finished` or `cancelled`, when it left (`at_ms`, Unix milliseconds) and how long it took, the tokens the provider reported, and once it returned what it settled (`cost`). Each member is present only when its producer reported it.

SessionCallCost.description: What a finished call cost, as the Session settled the requests it returned: `priced` at the sum of their known estimates (`nano_usd`, a decimal string of nano-USD at the route's list price: an estimate, never an invoice), or `unpriced` when one returned with no price. Absent while the call runs, when nothing settled, and when its producer states nothing. A host sums the priced calls for a live preparation cost and counts the unpriced beside it.

SessionTool.description: One tool the conversation's intelligence called, as its run observed it — never its arguments: the call's identity, the tool, `started`, `finished` or `failed`, the milliseconds it took once it answered, and once it failed why (`reply`).

reply.description: failed only: the tool's reply as a host may show it, its obvious secret shapes redacted first (API keys, private key blocks, password, token and secret values), on one line, at most 512 bytes and cut marked …

SessionVerification.description: Original compiler semantic_verification records retained by a ready proposal. A tool activity binds this receipt to its enclosing Session and command. No field grants admission or proves a Run. Request and context identities belong to each original record. candidate_revision is the local conversation revision, not a document base hash. reused means this proposal reuses a previous verification rather than invoking one. These original records may first become visible here; it does not mean their calls never happened. Do not add their call counts again when seen repeatedly.

records.description: The complete compiler attempt array, unchanged, including unsuccessful attempts and original consumed/read_back fields. Omitted with the receipt when the producer's secret-shape check would alter it.

SessionOutcome.description: One TurnOutcome, projected mechanically: reply, facts, help, aside, ask, cancelled (with `withdrawn` outcomes when a Stop withdrew a late result), stopped (a turn of the conversation the selected intelligence leads, stopped by the person: `reach` `between_steps`, `request_dropped` (a request already sent may still be billed) or `agent_cancelled` (the agent was asked once, `session/cancel`), `unsent` queued lines, `candidate` the draft revision kept), quit, refusal (`class`), held and proposal (`proposal`), question (`key`), gate (`trace`, `task`; `values`: the values its message renders, by key, as one object; `withheld`: the keys whose value it withheld, each with why: `secret` (derived from a secret), `size` or `unresolved`), run_requested (`workflow`, `inputs` names only, `max_cost_usd`), resume_requested (`workflow`, `trace`, `answer`), run_review (`review`: the run waits at its fresh cost review), run_reviewed, run_not_started (nothing ran), run_unobserved (admitted, its end not observed: effects unknown), run_stopped (a Stop reached the run and it sealed its trace as cancelled), run_aborted (a Stop reached the run but it ended without sealing its trace: cut mid-flight, effects in flight unknown), resumed, other. A kind this list does not name is shown as unknown, never guessed.

event.description: present on frames of the log; a replayed result keeps its original event
